FN-QI0R44-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 86
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: JT Mathis Date: 05/03/2023
Senate Bill 86 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education would provide
a one-time tax refundable income tax credit to partially offset the amount of sales tax paid on
groceries for certain qualified taxpayers who have filed an individual income tax return for the
2021 taxable year. This bill provides that the amount of the tax credit shall be equal to $105 for
taxpayers that are married filing separate, head of family, or single and $210 for taxpayers that
are married filing jointly and shall not constitute taxable income for Alabama income tax
purposes.
According to the Department of Revenue, this would increase the obligations of the Education
Trust Fund by an estimated $273 million for fiscal year 2023 only.
Further, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of the Department by an
estimated $1.1 million to mail one-time tax credit checks to approximately 1.9 million qualified
individual taxpayers.

FN-QI0R44-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 86
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: JT Mathis Date: 05/03/2023
Senate Bill 86 as introduced would provide a one-time tax rebate check for certain qualified
taxpayers who have filed an individual income tax return for the 2021 taxable year. The amount
of the rebate shall be equal to $400 for taxpayers that are married filing separate, head of family,
or single and $800 for taxpayers that are married filing jointly.
According to the Department of Revenue, this would increase the obligations of the Education
Trust Fund by an estimated $1 billion for fiscal year 2023 only.
Further, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of the Department by an
estimated $1.1 million to mail one-time rebate checks to approximately 1.9 million qualified
individual taxpayers.

FN-QI0R44-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 86
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: JT Mathis Date: 05/19/2023
Senate Bill 86 as passed the Senate would increase the obligations of the Education Trust Fund
by an estimated $273 million for fiscal year 2023 by providing a one-time refundable income
tax credit to certain qualified individual income taxpayers to partially offset the amount of sales
tax paid on groceries in an amount equal to: (1) $105 for taxpayers that are married filing
separate, head of family, or single; or (2) $210 for taxpayers that are married filing jointly. This
bill would provide that this credit shall not constitute taxable income for Alabama income tax
purposes.
Further, this bill would increase the obligations of the Department of Revenue by an estimated
$1.1 million in fiscal year 2023 to mail these tax credit checks to approximately 1.9 million
taxpayers within 90 days of the effective date of this bill.

FN-QI0R44-4
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 86
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: JT Mathis Date: 05/24/2023
Senate Bill 86 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means Education would increase the
obligations of the Education Trust Fund by an estimated $546 million for fiscal year 2023 by
providing a one-time refundable income tax credit check to certain qualified individual income
taxpayers to partially offset the amount of sales tax paid on groceries in an amount equal to: (1)
$210 for taxpayers that are married filing separate, head of family, or single; or (2) $420 for
taxpayers that are married filing jointly. This bill would provide that this credit shall not
constitute taxable income for Alabama income tax purposes.
Further, this bill would increase the obligations of the Department of Revenue by an estimated
$1.1 million in fiscal year 2023 to mail these tax credit checks to approximately 1.9 million
taxpayers within 90 days of the effective date of this bill.
